title: the MCP servers of a session speak HTTP
intent: No agent of Yeah could run inside the orchestrator Paseo, and the reason was in the transport of MCP and not in the model, not in the tools and not in the wire of ACP.  The kernel spoke the stdio transport of MCP and no other (wave 43e), and Paseo names its own MCP server over HTTP: the orchestrator hands the agent an MCP server of the shape `{type: http, url: http://127.0.0.1:6767/mcp/agents?callerAgentId=..., headers: [{name: Authorization, value: Bearer ...}]}' (packages/plugin/src/server/acp-internal/connection.ts, `toAcpMcpServers'; packages/server/src/server/agent/runtime-mcp-config.ts, `withRuntimePaseoMcpServer').  The kernel answered such a name with a refusal by name -- `Yeah speaks stdio only' -- and the session was refused before a single token was spent.  The live run of 2026-11-19 through the UI of Paseo died on exactly that line: `Error: Failed to create agent: the MCP server paseo speaks http; Yeah speaks stdio only'.  What changes: the transport of MCP is a property of the agent and not a property of the plugin, so it is fixed in the kernel.  The core speaks stdio and HTTP now, and it declares that in the handshake of ACP (`mcpCapabilities: {http: true, sse: false}').  The new module `lib/yeah-mcp-http.el' is a minimal asynchronous HTTP/1.1 client on `make-network-process': it reads the socket as binary (the sizes of the chunks of HTTP are measured in bytes), it parses the head (the status, the headers, `content-length' and `transfer-encoding: chunked'), it decodes the chunks, it reads the events of the server-sent events of MCP, it hands every JSON-RPC message to the client and it closes the socket after the message that carries an `id' (the server of MCP over HTTP of the SDK of the orchestrator keeps no state, so its stream does not end by itself).  The bytes become text in one place only (`lib/yeah-text.el'), so a byte that is not text cannot kill the process (wave 45).  The headers `Mcp-Session-Id' and `MCP-Protocol-Version' are supported, so a server that keeps a state works too.  The transport `sse' is refused by name, and so is `https': the kernel has no TLS.  The check starts a real ACP service on a socket, opens a session that names an MCP server over HTTP (the server of the check is the shape of the server of Paseo: stateless, the answer comes as the stream of the events of MCP over HTTP), and proves four things on the wire: the session is answered and not refused; the tools of the server reach the model and the model calls one of them; the call of the model reaches the server; the header the client named reaches the server too.  The number of the wave is the next free one: the wave is outside the plan of the owner (the point P-A of the plan of the integration with the orchestrator, docs/PASEO-INTEGRATION-PLAN.md 3.7), and the owner may rename it.
objection: The check proves the transport of the kernel and not the route through the orchestrator: the live run through the UI of Paseo after this wave is not the proof of this wave, and the wave says so.  The transport is HTTP/1.1 and no TLS: a server that answers `https' is refused by name (`Yeah speaks http only'), and that is a limit of the kernel, not a choice of taste -- Emacs has no TLS socket of its own.  The transport `sse' of MCP is refused by name too (`Yeah speaks stdio and http only'), and the stream of the events is read inside the answer of HTTP and not as a transport of its own.  The client of the HTTP transport closes the socket after the message that carries an `id', which is right for a stateless server and is wrong for a server that pushes the notifications after the answer: such a server needs the session id of `Mcp-Session-Id' and a socket that stays open, and the kernel keeps that header and sends it, but the check does not cover a server that pushes after the answer.  The transport answers no HTTP status of its own: a 401 of the orchestrator (a capability token that is missing or wrong) is a refusal of the transport, and the wave does not pretend that the kernel can fix a token it is not given.  The refusal of a transport that is not stdio and not http is still a refusal of the whole session, and a client that names such a server gets no session at all.
refuted_by: the session with an MCP server over HTTP is refused, or the handshake of the server never comes, or the model of the session finds no tool of the server, or the call of the model does not reach the server, or the headers of the client do not reach the server, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The subject of the claim: the session that names an MCP server over HTTP is answered with a session id, the model of that session finds the tool of the server among the tools of its run and calls it, the call of the model reaches the server, the header the client named reaches the server, and the client of the session saw the call of the tool on the wire.  The control of the claim (`sed -i 's|(yeah-mcp-http--events client)|nil|' lib/yeah-mcp-http.el') was applied to a copy of the tree and bit: the check ended with the code 1 and with its own words -- `the wire refused the session with an MCP server over HTTP: ... did not answer the handshake in 10 seconds' and `the model of the session did not use the tool of the server'.  The check costs about a second.  The stdio path did not move: `check-the-mcp-servers-of-a-session-reach-the-model.el' is still green.  The defect this wave repairs was found by a live run through the orchestrator and not by a check: `paseo run --provider yeah' died on `the MCP server paseo speaks http; Yeah speaks stdio only' (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md, the live run of 2026-11-19).
